mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation index above 0.3% triggers a preemptive S&P 500 forward return anticipation as investors price in rate hikes before the FED responds.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 0.3 in the preceding month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero when CPIAUCSL > 0.3, or FEDFUNDS does not rise within 30 days.

mechanism_narrative: Rising employment momentum as measured by PAYEMS suggests labor market strength, which precedes S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days by reducing risk aversion.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns under PAYEMS > 1.5% growth are negative or flat, or UNRATE does not decline accordingly.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates weakening aggregate demand, which predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive despite INDPRO falling for 2 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous drop in both GDPC1 (goods demand) and RSAFS (retail sales) indicates supply-side constraints, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over 20 days as market anticipates price relief.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significant (p > 0.10) or both proxies revert to growth within 10 days.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS rises by more than 0.25% in a month, it signals tightening and predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days as discount rates rise.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive or flat despite FEDFUNDS increase, or other inflation proxies do not rise.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in UNRATE over 3 months reduces policy uncertainty and is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative when UNRATE decline is not followed by SPX outperformance.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in HOUST (housing starts) above the prior year's January level, occurring during a non-recession regime, predicts positive 5-day S&P 500 forward returns as optimism about construction fuels equity valuations.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns negative despite HOUST surge, or broader economic indicators contradict the signal.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent weakness in both PAYEMS (labor) and INDPRO (industries) suggests dual softness that triggers negative S&P 500 forward returns over 20 days as market anticipates recession risk.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative or proxies revert to growth within 10 days.
